d1.title: Vitamin D and acute respiratory tract infection
d1.text: A meta-analysis of 25 randomised controlled trials found that vitamin D supplementation reduced the risk of acute respiratory tract infection, with the largest effect in participants with baseline deficiency.

d2.title: Vitamin D dosing regimens
d2.text: Bolus dosing of vitamin D did not show a protective effect against respiratory infection, whereas daily or weekly supplementation did.

d3.title: Calcium supplementation and bone density
d3.text: Calcium supplementation increased bone mineral density modestly in postmenopausal women; vitamin D co-administration was common.

d4.title: Intermittent fasting and metabolic health
d4.text: Alternate day fasting improved insulin sensitivity in adults with obesity over a twelve week intervention, independent of total weight loss.

d5.title: Time restricted eating trial
d5.text: Eight hour time restricted eating produced a small improvement in fasting insulin among adults, but no change in HbA1c.

d6.title: Ketogenic diets and glycaemic control
d6.text: Low carbohydrate ketogenic diets lowered fasting glucose in adults with type 2 diabetes.

d7.title: Sparse attention for long documents
d7.text: We introduce a sparse attention mechanism that scales transformer retrieval models to documents of tens of thousands of tokens.

d8.title: Dense passage retrieval
d8.text: Dense passage retrieval with dual encoders outperforms BM25 on open domain question answering benchmarks.

d9.title: Attention is not explanation
d9.text: We examine whether transformer attention weights can be interpreted as explanations of model predictions.

d10.title: Nutrition labelling policy
d10.text: Front of package nutrition labelling changed purchasing behaviour in a supermarket field experiment.

d11.title: Sleep duration and immunity
d11.text: Short sleep duration was associated with increased susceptibility to the common cold in a prospective cohort.

d12.title: Zinc lozenges and cold duration
d12.text: Zinc lozenges shortened the duration of the common cold by about one day in pooled trials.
